properties.name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
properties.desc: The Persian Empire at its greatest extent, from Egypt and Thrace to the Indus.

sources.cite: Ancient World Mapping Center (UNC), after the Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000)

properties.name: Empire of Alexander
properties.desc: Alexander's conquests at his death in 323 BC.

sources.cite: Ancient World Mapping Center (UNC), after the Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000)

properties.name: Roman Republic
properties.desc: Roman territory around 60 BC, after Pompey's eastern settlement and before Caesar finished conquering Gaul.

sources.cite: Plutarch, Life of Pompey; Caesar, Gallic War
Ancient World Mapping Center (UNC), after the Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000)

properties.name: Roman Empire
properties.desc: The empire at its greatest extent under Trajan, including the short-lived provinces of Armenia, Mesopotamia and Assyria.

sources.cite: Ancient World Mapping Center (UNC), after the Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000)

properties.name: Roman Empire
properties.desc: The empire under the Severans around AD 200, including Dacia and Septimius Severus's province of Mesopotamia.

sources.cite: Ancient World Mapping Center (UNC), after the Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000)

properties.name: Kingdom of David and Solomon
properties.desc: The united kingdom of Israel as described in 2 Samuel 5–8 and 1 Kings 4. Archaeologists disagree about its size and how centralized it was: some see a substantial state ruled from Jerusalem, others a smaller highland kingdom. Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

sources.cite: Tel Dan stele (9th c. BC), naming the 'House of David'
I. Finkelstein and N. A. Silberman, The Bible Unearthed (2001)
K. A. Kitchen, On the Reliability of the Old Testament (2003)

properties.name: Solomon's dominion (as 1 Kings describes it)
properties.desc: 1 Kings 4:21–24 says Solomon ruled 'from the River (Euphrates) to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt', and 1 Kings 9:26 places his fleet at Ezion-geber on the Red Sea. The dashed line shows that description; no independent inscription confirms rule this far.

properties.name: Kingdom of Israel
properties.desc: The northern kingdom after the division under Jeroboam I (1 Kings 12). Under the Omride kings it held Gilead east of the Jordan and dominated Moab, as both the Bible and the Moabite king Mesha record. Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

sources.cite: Kurkh Monolith of Shalmaneser III, naming Ahab at Qarqar (853 BC)
Samaria ostraca; Megiddo and Hazor excavations

properties.name: Kingdom of Israel (reduced)
properties.desc: After Tiglath-pileser III annexed Galilee and Gilead (2 Kings 15:29), Israel was left with the hill country around Samaria until Assyria destroyed it in 722/720 BC. Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

properties.name: Kingdom of Judah
properties.desc: The southern kingdom ruled by the house of David from Jerusalem until the Babylonian destruction. Its southern reach changed over time; Edom broke away under Jehoram (2 Kings 8:20–22). Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

sources.cite: Lachish letters (ostraca written during the Babylonian invasion, c. 588 BC)

properties.name: Philistia
properties.desc: The five Philistine cities of Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron and Gath (Joshua 13:3; 1 Samuel 6:17). Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Ashkelon in 604 BC. Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

sources.cite: Medinet Habu reliefs of Ramesses III (the Peleset)

properties.name: Moab
properties.desc: East of the Dead Sea between the Arnon and the Zered (Numbers 21:13; Deuteronomy 2). Its king Mesha boasted of freeing Moab from Israel. Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

properties.name: Ammon
properties.desc: Kingdom centred on Rabbah (modern Amman), bounded by the Jabbok river (Deuteronomy 3:16). Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

properties.name: Edom
properties.desc: Highland kingdom south of the Dead Sea down to the Gulf of Aqaba, refused Israel passage in Numbers 20. Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

sources.cite: Khirbet en-Nahas copper mines (T. Levy and M. Najjar)

properties.name: Aram-Damascus
properties.desc: Aramaean kingdom ruled from Damascus, Israel's chief rival in the 9th century BC, conquered by Tiglath-pileser III in 732 BC (2 Kings 16:9). Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

properties.name: Phoenicia (Tyre and Sidon)
properties.desc: The coastal cities of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos. Hiram of Tyre supplied cedar for Solomon's temple (1 Kings 5). Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

properties.name: Province of Yehud (Judah under Persia)
properties.desc: The small Persian province around Jerusalem resettled by returning exiles under Cyrus's decree; Nehemiah rebuilt its walls. Outline drawn by hand for this atlas from the biblical boundary descriptions and the excavated sites; accurate only to tens of kilometres.

sources.cite: Elephantine papyri (petition to Bagohi, governor of Yehud, 407 BC)

properties.name: Hasmonean kingdom
properties.desc: The Jewish kingdom at its widest under Alexander Jannaeus (103–76 BC), before Pompey's conquest in 63 BC. Outline from the Ancient World Mapping Center (Barrington Atlas).

sources.cite: Ancient World Mapping Center, after the Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000)

properties.name: Kingdom of Herod the Great
properties.desc: The Roman client kingdom of Herod the Great. Jesus was born near the end of his reign (Matthew 2:1). Outline from the Ancient World Mapping Center (Barrington Atlas).

sources.cite: Ancient World Mapping Center, after the Barrington Atlas
